title: Promises
explain: A Promise is a JavaScript object that represents a value that may not be available yet but will be resolved in the future. Promises have three states: pending (waiting), fulfilled (completed successfully), or rejected (failed). You can use .then() to handle the result when a Promise settles.
exercise: Create a Promise that rejects after 500ms with the message 'Operation failed', then add a .catch() handler to log the error message.
tip: Don't forget that .then() and .catch() return new Promises—this is what allows method chaining. Also, a Promise can only settle once, so calling resolve() or reject() multiple times has no effect.
